## Short answer

No. Do not pin exact versions in one shared `requirements.txt`. The two roles need opposite answers, so write two artifacts.

- **Library contract** → `pyproject.toml`, `[project] dependencies`, ranges only.
- **Service deploy** → `requirements.lock.txt`, generated, exact pins plus hashes.

## Why the split

A library states which versions it *can* work with. It must not choose the version. `pip` resolves one version of each package for the whole environment. An exact pin in library metadata creates a conflict when another installed package needs a different version. The consuming team then cannot install both packages. That pin also gives them no safety, because they resolve their own environment anyway.

A service owns its whole environment. Exact versions make the build identical on every machine. Hashes add a second property: they block a package substitution at install time. A pin costs the service nothing.

## Range policy

Write a lower bound for every dependency, set at the oldest version you test against. Add an upper bound only when you know of a real break. A speculative cap such as `<3` is itself a source of conflict for consumers, and it locks them out of a release that may work.

## What this repo needs today

`fixture/rotate_logs.py` imports the standard library only. There is no `requirements.txt`, no `pyproject.toml`, and no lockfile. The only third-party need is `pytest`, for `fixture/tests/test_rotate_logs.py`. So there is nothing to migrate. This is scaffolding, and now is the cheapest moment to set it up.

One verification step is worth calling out. After you generate the lockfile, corrupt one hash character in a copy of it, then run `pip install --require-hashes -r <copy>`. Confirm that the install fails. Without `--require-hashes` the hashes are decoration, and this test is the only thing that proves the check is live.

**Open decision for you:** apply this now as scaffolding, or wait for the first real dependency. I recommend now. The cost is one small `pyproject.toml`. The alternative is a retrofit under time pressure, after a consumer team reports a conflict.
